All conformal prediction methods are evaluated in terms of empirical coverage and average prediction set size. Marginal coverage reports the fraction of prediction sets that contain the true label for labeled examples in the test set 𝒟 test \mathcal{D}_{\textrm{test}} . We estimate empirical coverage as reported either averaged per-task, or averaged jointly over all tasks. Eventhough SCOS and CAOS enjoy finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees, it can still occur that individual results lie below the target coverage of 1 − α 1-\alpha . This is particularly prone to happen for small test sets 𝒟 test \mathcal{D}_{\textrm{test}} .
